style: Icon-focused accent animation, not a real map — a generic abstract 3x3 grid of stylized 'zone' cells (line-art, rounded squares) standing in for a targeting/map metaphor. Purple/black brand system, restrained motion, one dominant motif per beat, no decorative glows beyond the specified landing pulse.

customize.note: No catalog block matched an abstract zone-grid + pin-drop-landing accent (searched 'grid of zones highlight target cell map pin drop' and 'map pin marker drop bounce landing icon' — closest hits were us-map-hex/us-map-bubble/pin-rollout, all real-geography US map blocks, wrong fit for a generic non-geographic icon accent). Logged via hyperframes feedback --search-miss. Hand-authored per categories/maps/module.md vector-lane signatures (pin drop + pulse ring) using hand-drawn line-art SVG, not the US map family.

shot_brief: A clean 3x3 grid of muted zone cells fades and scales into frame in a quiet stagger, all reading as roughly equal. Two specific cells then brighten into the accent purple — a clear 'these are the good ones' contrast beat while the rest recede further into shadow. A simple line-art map-pin icon falls from above and lands on the brightest (center) cell with a small bounce and a glow-pulse ring, visually confirming the target. A short punchy label fades in beneath — TARGETED, NOT SCATTERED. — and the frame holds for a clean cut. One motif per beat: fade/stagger-in, then color contrast, then pin landing, then label; the persistent bg-fill never drops to empty.
